newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila sees sugar consumption to rise 4 - 5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Manila sees sugar consumption to rise 4 - 5 pct.

text.p: Domestic sugar consumption is projected to increase four to five percent every year starting crop year 1997/98, starting September, Sugar Regulatory Administration chief Wilson Gamboa said on Wednesday.
Gamboa, in a statement released by the presidential palace, said the rise was in line with a growing local economy.

"Gamboa viewed domestic sugar consumption to be increasing at a fantastic rate of four to five percent annually, indicating an improving quality of life brought about by the growth of the country's economy," the statement said.
This year, sugar consumption was estimated at 1.82 million tonnes, 40,000 tonnes lower than the projected domestic output of 1.86 million.
The oversupply was exacerbated by importation earlier this year, which put several local sugar mills in financial trouble.
Gamboa said the oversupply will be fully consumed by August, the end of the present crop year.
